newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury's one-year bills seen at 5.20 percent.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury's one-year bills seen at 5.20 percent.

text.p: The U.S. Treasury's sale of $19.5 billion in 52-week bills is expected to go at an average rate of 5.20 percent.

"This auction should not be a problem," said William Sullivan, senior vice president and head of fixed-income market research at Dean Witter Reynolds. "Bills are bills; if you can't sell them, you might as well close up shop."
Traders said the bills were likely to be sold at an average rate somewhere between 5.18 percent and 5.20 percent.
A half hour before the 1130 EST/1630 GMT bidding deadline, year bills were trading at a when-issued rate of 5.20 percent.
